seo.description: How the Tulsi Heera Foundation started after the 2015 Nepal earthquake, and why we now help any child who needs support to stay in school.
seo.title: About

story.text:
In 2015 a huge earthquake hit Nepal. Sindhupalchowk was one of the worst-hit districts. We collected some money and went to visit the villages around Chautara.

We met many children who had lost their families and were now living with relatives. Some of these relatives were so poor that the children were not going to school, even though a year at a government school cost only about 3,000 rupees at the time.

The money we had collected was not much, so we decided to use it for what mattered most: paying for these children to go to school.

At first we helped only children affected by the earthquake. Then the village leaders in Chautara and the school headmaster told us that many organisations were already helping earthquake victims, while other poor and orphaned children were getting no help at all.

So we changed. Since then we have supported any child who needs help to stay in school, whether or not the earthquake affected them.

Many children in Sindhupalchowk have lost one or both parents. Others live with families who cannot afford the yearly school fees.

We pay those fees so the children can stay in school. We have done this every year since 2015.

hero.text: In short: this website uses no cookies, does not track you and has no forms. We only get your details if you call us or message us.
hero.title: Privacy and cookies

seo.description: This website uses no cookies and does not track you. How we handle your details when you call us or message us on WhatsApp.
seo.title: Privacy and cookies

i1.text: We use only the first names of the children in our stories. If you are a parent or guardian and want a story changed or removed, contact us.
i1.title: Children in our stories

i2.text: If you call us or message us on WhatsApp, we see your phone number and anything you choose to tell us, such as your name. We use it only to answer you, arrange your donation and send your donation certificate. We do not sell it, and we only share it if the law requires us to. WhatsApp is run by Meta, which has its own privacy policy.
i2.title: When you call or message us

i3.text: This website does not use cookies and does not save anything on your device. We do not use analytics, advertising or any other tracking. That is why you do not see a cookie banner.
i3.title: Cookies

i4.text: Like all websites, ours runs on a hosting provider's servers. These may keep basic technical logs, such as IP addresses and the pages visited, to keep the site working and safe. We do not use these logs to identify you.
i4.title: Website hosting

i5.text: You can ask us what information we have about you, and ask us to correct it or delete it. If you live in the European Union, you can also complain to your data protection authority. In Spain, this is the AEPD (Spanish Data Protection Agency).
i5.title: Your rights

i6.text: To thank them, we list some of our supporters by name. If you are on the list and want your name removed, or want it added, tell us and we will change it.
i6.title: Our supporters' names

i7.text: The videos on our Stories page are hosted on YouTube, which belongs to Google. A video does not load until you press play. Once you do, YouTube receives your IP address and may save cookies on your device, under Google's own privacy policy.
i7.title: Videos from YouTube

i8.text: This website belongs to the Tulsi Heera Foundation, based in Kathmandu, Nepal. If you have a question about your information, call us or message us on WhatsApp using the contact details at the bottom of this page.
i8.title: Who runs this website
